summary: Intermittent 5xx sawtooth during evening keepalive churn; upstream runtime GPU OOMs
description: Issue summary: Beginning ~2026-03-13 18:15 PDT we observed a repeating sawtooth pattern of elevated 5xx responses on a small set of routes serving VoltCommerce (dedicated tenant). Errors manifest as 502/503 from the API gateway with corresponding runtime exits on a subset of serving hosts. Impact: Several VoltCommerce production customers reporting increased failed requests for chat and embeddings over an ~2 hour window; throughput degraded and tail latency increased >3x. Environment: prod us-west-2, dedicated pool (tenant-voltcommerce-reserved). Immediate symptoms: API gateway 502 spikes aligned with keepalive connection churn; runtimes show GPU OOM events and watchdog restarts. Steps to reproduce (observed): repeated small-interval client reconnects + long-lived streaming sessions from VoltCommerce SDK reproduce an accept-queue surge in our staging harness and cause the same runtime OOM pattern.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) With a dedicated tenant config, open ~600 concurrent streaming sessions from single IP using VoltCommerce SDK v2.1 with keepalive interval 15s
2) Send short prompts (~50 tokens) in bursts (10 reqs/sec per connection) for 5-10 minutes
3) Observe apigw accept queue growth, keepalive half-open sockets increase, and runtime prefetch cancellation events
4) After a delay, runtime initiates background NVMe snapshot (observed on affected hosts) which coincides with a GPU memory spike and subsequent cuda OOM / process kill
5) API gateway surfaces 502/503 for in-flight requests while runtime restarts
logs: [2026-03-13T18:17:12Z] runtime-serve[pid=4231]: cuda: out of memory when allocating 512MB (free=48MB) -> SIGABRT
[2026-03-13T18:17:13Z] systemd: runtime-serve.service: main process exited, code=killed, status=6/ABRT
[2026-03-13T18:17:14Z] apigw: returning 502 to client (upstream closed) route=/v1/chat/stream tenant=voltcommerce
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: keepalive/reconnect storm causes apigw accept queue growth, causing many short-lived handoffs to runtimes and frequent prefetch cancellations. Prefetch cancellation + high socket churn increases memory pressure in serving runtime. On affected hosts we observed background nvme snapshot compaction starting concurrently with peak churn which appears to delay disk I/O and trigger higher pinned GPU memory (shard rehydration path). The combination pushes runtime GPU allocation past threshold and triggers cuda OOM. Evidence: host metrics (link below) show GPU memory climbing ~10% immediately after nvme compaction started; dmesg shows NVML logs and CUDA OOM. Mitigations attempted: temporary tenant rate cap (applied at 18:22) reduced accept queue depth and error rate; rolling restart of two affected runtime instances removed hosts stuck in crash loop. Current working theory: two correlated factors (excessive keepalive churn + coincident nvme background task) produce transient resource spike. Follow-ups: schedule nvme snapshot compaction outside peak hours for dedicated pools, add apigw early-shed for high keepalive churn, and add guardrail in serving runtime to fail fast on prefetch-heavy sequences to avoid OOM.
